answer: Operator collateral clawback: each agent identity registers against an operator-held collateral pool that is seized, not slashed per-wallet, when any identity in its cohort is proven fake. Enforcement runs on a dune of accumulated flags: once flagged identities in a cohort exceed a threshold, the entire pool is liquidated and the operator is barred from registering new cohorts until it reposts at a rising knoll of required collateral. The tide of re-registration costs rises with each offense, so an attacker pays full pool loss plus escalating entry prices per identity.
